inlines.v: TRI'ABLE, adjective [from try.] That may be tried; that may be subjected to trial or test. 1. That may undergo a judicial examination; that may properly come under the cognizance of a court. A cause may be triable before one court, which is not triable in another. In England, testamentary causes are triable in the ecclesiastical courts.
